gen-megrim-gf-armata: Futuristic and angular, Megrim draws every stroke at a single measured thickness, thin as bent wire. And Armata, a plain sans with spacious gaps between its characters, is the part of the pair that lets the text breathe.
gen-megrim-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible: Megrim's strokes stay constant as bent wire, with an angular, futuristic edge that never thickens at the curves. Atkinson Hyperlegible does the opposite job: approachable, wide-set terminals on its s.
gen-megrim-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible-mono: Megrim's c is as open as a bent paperclip, and every stroke ends at the same measured thickness. Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono, a sans-serif with wide stencil-bridge spacing, probably wants a generous size so its open counters can breathe.
gen-megrim-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible-next: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next reads friendly and current, its lowercase eyes as big as washers and its rounds left unlatched like a hook. Its strongest quality is how that openness sits beside Megrim's wiry angles.
gen-megrim-gf-biryani: Megrim's skyward x-height line and wire-thin angular strokes give it a futuristic look all its own. And Biryani, a sans-serif with large eyes on every e, keeps a long passage unclogged and approachable.
gen-megrim-gf-blinker: Sharp, wiry, a bit sci-fi: that is Megrim, with an open c and a skyward x-height line. Blinker, a plain sans, does the quieter job, holding its line thickness steady while open apertures make the text easy to follow.
gen-megrim-gf-carrois-gothic: Carrois Gothic is a modern sans with a high-set x-height and a generous opening in its c, set under Megrim's angular display lettering. And a longer passage would move along smoothly, since Megrim's curves are as thick as its straight stems.
gen-megrim-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Megrim never varies its stroke weight, so its angular, futuristic letters look cut from a single bent wire. Carrois Gothic SC, a sans-serif with clear openings at the end of every curve, would carry a longer passage in a contemporary, approachable way.
gen-megrim-gf-chivo: Megrim opens this pair with angular, futuristic lettering whose plain, unshaded line never swells. Chivo, a plain sans with lowercase packed up toward the caps, would let a longer passage read steadily, daylight showing through every curve.
gen-megrim-gf-chocolate-classical-sans: Megrim has no thick-and-thin modulation at all, just angular, futuristic strokes ending at one measured thickness. Chocolate Classical Sans, a plain sans with a sizable lowercase, would read a longer passage smoothly.
